text: {"question":"Which cosmological model—dark QCD with its characteristic scale ΛD or early dark energy injection—offers a better fit to the combined Lyman‑α and CMB data while also addressing the Hubble tension, and why does one outperform the other?","reference_answer":"Early dark energy injection outperforms dark QCD because it achieves a closer match to the Lyman‑α power spectrum and reduces the Hubble tension more effectively, whereas dark QCD, despite its distinct ΛD‑driven oscillations, remains in significant tension with Lyman‑α measurements and does not resolve the Hubble discrepancy as well.","passage_1_contribution":"Dark QCD’s oscillation scale is governed by ΛD, yet it shows strong tension with Lyman‑α data.","passage_2_contribution":"Early dark energy injection ranks highest in resolving the Hubble tension and fits CMB and low‑redshift data better than other mechanisms.","joint_reason":"Both passages discuss how different models perform against Lyman‑α and Hubble‑tension datasets, allowing a direct comparison of their effectiveness.","same_quantity":false}
